questions.q:
With reference to drone-swarm systems, consider the following pairs:
System : Country
1. Atlas : China
2. Perdix : United States
3. Bhargavastra : India
4. KARGU : Israel
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Atlas, unveiled in 2026, is an AI-enabled swarm system of a Chinese state electronics group. Perdix is an American micro-drone swarm. Bhargavastra is Indian, but note that it is a counter-swarm system meant to destroy incoming drones. Pair 4 is wrong: KARGU is a Turkish loitering-munition swarm. Israel has a separate swarm defence system of its own.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the SMILE mission, launched in 2026, is correct?
o: It is a NASA-ISRO radar mission to map changes in the Earth's ice sheets and crust.
It is a European-Japanese mission that will orbit Mercury to study its magnetic field.
It is a NASA probe that flies through the Sun's corona to sample the solar wind at source.
It is a joint mission of the European Space Agency and the Chinese Academy of Sciences to image how the solar wind interacts with the Earth's magnetosphere.
questions.e: SMILE stands for Solar wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer. Launched on a Vega-C rocket from French Guiana, it carries the first space-borne soft X-ray imager to show the boundaries of the magnetosphere, along with an ultraviolet aurora imager, a magnetometer and an ion analyser. The aim is to understand space weather such as geomagnetic storms. The other descriptions fit NISAR, BepiColombo and the Parker Solar Probe.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Orbital data centres are proposed as a way of reducing the environmental footprint of AI computing.
Statement-II: Data centres on the ground use large quantities of fresh water for cooling.
Statement-III: A satellite in a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit receives almost uninterrupted sunlight on its solar panels.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: Both later statements are correct and both explain the first. On the ground a mid-sized computing cluster can use over a million tonnes of water a year and draws heavily on the grid, so moving the load to orbit saves water. In a dawn-dusk orbit the satellite rides the boundary between day and night, so its panels are almost always lit, and waste heat is radiated to cold space without any water. Together they support the claim of a smaller environmental footprint.

questions.q: In 2026 an international panel renamed polycystic ovary syndrome as 'polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome'. The main reason given was that
o: ovarian cysts have been shown to be the cause of, and not a result of, excess androgens
many patients do not have ovarian cysts, and the condition involves several hormone systems and metabolic problems such as insulin resistance
the condition has been found to be caused by a virus and not by hormones
the condition affects men as often as women
questions.e: The old name pointed at cysts, which many patients lack, and so narrowed diagnosis and treatment. The new name stresses that several endocrine systems are involved, that insulin resistance and cardio-metabolic risk are central, and that irregular periods and problems of ovulation remain part of a multisystem syndrome. It is a common disorder of women of reproductive age marked by excess androgens; no viral cause has been found.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not correct about 'egocentric data', a term in the news in 2026?
o: Its collection has raised concerns about surveillance, consent and displacement of workers.
It refers to personal data that a user voluntarily posts about himself or herself on social media.
It is recorded from the first-person viewpoint of a person carrying out a task.
It is used to train vision-language-action models for robots.
questions.e: Egocentric data are video and sensor recordings from cameras worn on the head, chest or wrist, showing hand movements and handling of objects as the worker sees them. Because this matches a robot's own viewpoint, it is used to train models that join vision, language instructions and physical action. Workers may thus be recording the material that automates their jobs, hence the debate on consent, ownership and pay. It is unrelated to social-media posts.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
1. 'Vigyan Nidhi', a digital fellowship platform with direct benefit transfer
2. A National Institute for Science Policy and Governance
3. A Centre for Technology Indigenization
4. Raising research and development spending to at least 1 per cent of GDP within four to five years
How many of the above were recommended in NITI Aayog's report on ease of doing research and development, released in 2026?
questions.e: Items 1, 2 and 3 were recommended. The fellowship platform answers the long-standing complaint of delayed stipends. The policy institute, modelled on Japan's practice, would link policy with implementation and feedback. The indigenisation centre addresses the weak movement of research into products. Item 4 is wrong: India spends only about 0.65 per cent of GDP, and the report sets a target of at least 2 per cent, with about half coming from the private sector, so 1 per cent would be a modest aim.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not correct about the Cell Broadcast System launched in India in 2026?
o: It was launched by the Ministry of Communications.
It was developed indigenously by C-DOT with the National Disaster Management Authority and the Home Ministry.
People must install an application and register their mobile number to receive its alerts.
It is integrated with the SACHET alerting platform.
questions.e: No application or registration is needed: the network pushes the alert to all mobiles in a defined area, which is the whole point of broadcast. The other three are correct. The telecom research centre under the Department of Telecommunications built it with the disaster authority and the Home Ministry, and it works with the existing protocol-based alert platform. It complements impact-based weather forecasts by solving last-mile delivery.

questions.q:
With reference to the 79th World Health Assembly held in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It adopted the first resolution on radiation and health.
2. It adopted a strategy on the economics of health for all.
3. The Executive Board, and not the World Health Assembly, is the supreme decision-making body of the World Health Organization.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The resolution on radiation covers ionising and non-ionising radiation and asks countries to strengthen protection systems. The strategy for 2026 to 2030 asks governments to build health into economic, fiscal and industrial policy. Statement 3 is wrong: the Assembly, made up of all member States, meets every year in Geneva, sets WHO policy and approves its budget. The Executive Board, of 34 technically qualified members, only prepares the agenda and carries out the Assembly's decisions.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 113-114; WHA and Executive Board roles are static

questions.q: The 'Ayush Anudan Portal', launched in 2026 under the Ayush Grid, is meant to
o: sell Ayush medicines directly to consumers at regulated prices
register practitioners of Indian systems of medicine in a national register
digitise the submission, processing, approval and monitoring of grant proposals
issue quality certification for Ayush products meant for export
questions.e: 'Anudan' means grant: the portal moves the handling of grant proposals of the Ayush ministry online, from submission to monitoring. It is part of the Ayush Grid, a digital ecosystem begun by the ministry in 2018 that already includes a hospital management information system and e-Aushadhi, and that follows the standards of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. The other functions belong to different bodies and schemes.

questions.q:
With reference to access to research literature in India, consider the following statements:
Statement-I: NITI Aayog's 2026 report on research and development recommends that One Nation One Subscription be extended to private institutions.
Statement-II: One Nation One Subscription at present does not cover private institutions.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second is the reason for the first. The scheme gives publicly funded higher-education and research institutions access to major journals through a single national licence. Private universities and colleges, which enrol a large share of students, are outside it and face gaps in journals, databases and software. The report suggests bringing them in with cost-sharing, and building an open national repository and better Indian journals.

questions.q:
A hantavirus outbreak was reported in 2026. With reference to hantaviruses, consider the following statements:
1. They are transmitted to humans mainly through the bite of Aedes mosquitoes.
2. They affect only the kidneys and do not involve the lungs or the heart.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Hantaviruses are zoonotic viruses carried by rodents; people are infected through contact with rodents or their urine, droppings and saliva, often by breathing contaminated dust. They cause two syndromes: a rapidly progressing cardiopulmonary syndrome affecting lungs and heart, and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome. There is no specific cure, so care is supportive and prevention rests on rodent control.

questions.q:
With reference to hepatitis, on which the WHO issued a global report in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Hepatitis is caused only by viruses.
2. Hepatitis B and C are the commonest causes of cirrhosis and liver cancer.
3. Hepatitis D infects only those who also carry hepatitis B.
4. A vaccine is available against hepatitis C but not against hepatitis B.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. B and C cause chronic infection that scars the liver over years, and the D virus is incomplete and needs B to multiply. Statement 1 is wrong: alcohol, some drugs, other infections and autoimmune disease also inflame the liver. Statement 4 reverses the facts: there is an effective vaccine for B, given at birth, and none for C, which is instead curable with antivirals.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 115; hepatitis D and vaccine facts are static

questions.q:
Sweden joined India's Venus Orbiter Mission in 2026. With reference to the mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was approved in 2024 as India's first scientific mission to Venus.
2. The LVM-3 is the candidate launch vehicle.
3. It will place a lander and a rover on the surface of Venus.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The mission, planned for launch in March 2028, will be built and launched by ISRO, with the heavy-lift vehicle first placing the craft in an elliptical parking orbit around the Earth. Statement 3 is wrong: it is an orbiter. From orbit it will study the surface and subsurface, atmospheric processes and the effect of the Sun on the Venusian atmosphere.

questions.q:
With reference to foreign direct investment in India's space sector under the automatic route, consider the following pairs:
Activity : Limit
1. Manufacture of satellite components and sub-systems : 100 per cent
2. Satellite manufacturing and operation : 74 per cent
3. Launch vehicles : 74 per cent
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct; pair 3 is wrong. The liberalised policy grades the limit by strategic sensitivity: components and sub-systems are fully open, satellite manufacture and operation are open up to 74 per cent, and launch vehicles, the most sensitive segment because of their missile links, only up to 49 per cent, with government approval needed beyond these levels. The change followed the Indian Space Policy, 2023, which allowed private firms to take part end to end.

questions.q:
Chandrayaan-3 received the Goddard Astronautics Award in 2026. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The award is conferred by NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center.
2. Chandrayaan-3 made its soft landing near the lunar equator.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the award is the highest astronautics honour of the American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics, a professional society; both it and the NASA centre are named after Robert Goddard, the pioneer of liquid-fuel rockets. Statement 2 is wrong: on 23 August 2023 the Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole, the first soft landing so close to it, and not near the equator. The Pragyan rover then ran on solar power for about one lunar day.

questions.q:
In the context of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), consider the following statements:
1. The first global action plan on antimicrobial resistance was endorsed by the World Health Assembly in 2015.
2. The Quadripartite partnership that backs the One Health response to AMR comprises WHO, FAO, UNEP and UNICEF.
3. The Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS) is run by the Food and Agriculture Organization.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The World Health Assembly endorsed the first global action plan in 2015, and the 2026 session built on it. Statement 2 is wrong: the fourth Quadripartite member is the World Organisation for Animal Health, not UNICEF, which reflects the One Health link between people, animals and the environment. Statement 3 is wrong: GLASS is WHO's system for surveillance of resistance and antimicrobial use, which feeds national action plans such as India's, supported by the Red Line awareness campaign.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 113-114; 2015 plan, Quadripartite and GLASS as stated in the notes

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Initiative : Feature
1. National Quantum Mission : Thematic hub on quantum computing at IISc Bengaluru
2. National Quantum Mission : Thematic hub on quantum sensing and metrology at IIT Madras
3. National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems : Twenty-five Technology Innovation Hubs in leading institutions
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. The quantum mission has four thematic hubs; computing is at IISc Bengaluru, while sensing and metrology is at IIT Bombay, so pair 2 is wrong. IIT Madras hosts the hub on quantum communication. The cyber-physical systems mission works through 25 innovation hubs in institutions across the country. Both are cited as efforts to expand research capacity beyond a few central laboratories.

questions.q: The Vela Supercluster, mapped for the first time in 2026, had remained poorly known mainly because
o: it consists almost entirely of dark matter and emits no light
it lies behind the dust and stars of the Milky Way's disc
it is visible only from the polar regions of the Earth
it is too far away for its light to have reached the Earth
questions.e: The supercluster sits in the Zone of Avoidance, about a fifth of the sky where the Milky Way's own dust and stars block the view of galaxies beyond. It contains at least twenty galaxy clusters bound by gravity, lies some 800 million light-years away and is more massive than Laniakea, the supercluster that holds our galaxy. Its light does reach us; the difficulty was seeing through our own galaxy.

questions.q:
With reference to 'Pathfinder', described as India's first AI orbital data centre satellite, consider the following statements:
1. Pixxel is to build and operate the satellite, while Sarvam provides the AI backbone.
2. In orbit, its processors will be cooled mainly by convection of heat to the cold surroundings.
3. It is to carry data-centre-grade graphics processing units.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The satellite is a partnership between a space-technology firm and an AI start-up, and it carries high-performance processors of the kind used in data centres, unlike the low-power chips usual on satellites. Statement 2 is wrong: convection needs a fluid, and space is a near vacuum. Heat can leave a spacecraft only by radiation, through radiator panels facing deep space.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 108-109; heat transfer in vacuum is static

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes 'Bhargavastra'?
o: An Indian system designed to counter swarms of hostile drones
An Indian swarm of loitering munitions for deep strikes
An AI-enabled swarm warfare system unveiled by China in 2026
A hypersonic cruise missile powered by a scramjet engine
questions.e: Bhargavastra is a counter-swarm system: it is meant to detect and destroy many incoming drones at low cost. It should not be confused with India's own swarm projects, or with China's Atlas, the AI-enabled swarm system shown in 2026. As swarms become cheap and numerous, defence against them, through micro-missiles, jamming or directed energy, becomes as important as owning swarms.

questions.q:
With reference to Naegleria fowleri, the so-called brain-eating amoeba, consider the following statements:
1. It is a free-living organism found in soil and warm fresh water.
2. People are usually infected by drinking contaminated water.
3. It causes primary amoebic meningoencephalitis, an infection of the central nervous system.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The amoeba lives in warm lakes, ponds, rivers and hot springs, and the disease it causes is rare but progresses very fast and is nearly always fatal. Statement 2 is wrong: swallowing the water does not cause the disease. The organism enters through the nose during swimming or bathing and travels along the olfactory nerve to the brain. Warming waters may widen its range.

questions.q: TRAI issued a consultation paper in 2026 on a regulatory framework for vehicle-to-everything communication. Which one of the following correctly states the two competing technologies and TRAI's leaning?
o: Dedicated Short-Range Communication runs on 4G and 5G networks and C-V2X is Wi-Fi-based; the paper favours the former.
Both run on satellite links; the paper favours whichever offers India-wide coverage through NavIC.
Dedicated Short-Range Communication uses optical fibre along highways and C-V2X uses Bluetooth; the paper favours the latter.
Dedicated Short-Range Communication is Wi-Fi-based and C-V2X runs on cellular networks; the paper favours C-V2X.
questions.e: The older technology is a Wi-Fi-type short-range radio between vehicles and roadside units. Cellular V2X uses existing 4G and 5G networks and can also link vehicles to pedestrians and the wider network, so it is more comprehensive; the paper leans towards it. Regulation matters because interoperability, cyber-security, cost of roadside units and liability rules are unsettled. The safety case is collision warning and intersection management.

questions.q:
Satellites such as Drishti and Pathfinder use sun-synchronous low Earth orbits. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. Low Earth orbit extends up to an altitude of about 2,000 km.
2. A geostationary satellite orbits above the equator at roughly 36,000 km and takes about one day to complete an orbit.
3. A dawn-dusk sun-synchronous satellite crosses the equator near local noon on each pass.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Low Earth orbit runs from about 160 km to about 2,000 km, the band used by Drishti and Pathfinder. A geostationary satellite sits above the equator at about 36,000 km and its orbital period matches Earth's rotation, so it appears fixed over one spot. Statement 3 is wrong: a dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit crosses the equator near sunrise and sunset, which keeps the satellite on the day-night boundary and its panels almost always lit.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 108-109, 111; orbit definitions are static

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Indian firm)
A. Skyroot Aerospace
B. Agnikul Cosmos
C. Pixxel
D. GalaxEye
List-II (Known for)
1. Hyperspectral imaging satellites
2. India's first privately built rocket to be launched
3. A satellite combining optical and radar imaging
4. A rocket engine 3D-printed as a single piece
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Skyroot launched Vikram-S, the first private Indian rocket. Agnikul flew a semi-cryogenic engine printed in one piece, a world first. Pixxel's Firefly satellites image the Earth in hundreds of narrow bands to study crops, pollution and methane. GalaxEye built Drishti, which carries a multispectral camera and a synthetic aperture radar together. These firms show how the sector widened after it was opened to non-government entities in 2020.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 103-105; Vision IAS p. 111

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Atal Innovation Mission, launched in 2016, is housed in the Department of Science and Technology.
2. The Research Development and Innovation Scheme is intended to draw private-sector investment into deep-tech projects.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is wrong: the Atal Innovation Mission is a NITI Aayog initiative, known for tinkering labs in schools and incubation centres. Statement 2 is right. The scheme offers long-term, low-cost finance for cutting-edge projects and start-ups so that companies, which contribute a modest share of India's research spending, invest more. The research foundation under the science department has a similar aim of linking industry and academia.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 106-108; AIM's location is static

questions.q: DRDO ran an 'actively cooled' full-scale scramjet combustor for a long duration in 2026. In this context, active cooling means that
o: the combustor is coated with ablative material that chars and carries heat away
liquid oxygen carried on board is sprayed on the outer skin of the vehicle
air entering the intake is chilled by a heat exchanger before it is compressed
the fuel is circulated through channels in the combustor walls to absorb heat before it is burnt
questions.e: At hypersonic speed the combustor wall would melt within seconds. In active, or regenerative, cooling the hydrocarbon fuel flows through passages in the wall, takes up heat, and in the case of endothermic fuels breaks down chemically, absorbing still more, before being injected and burnt. Long run-times prove this works. An ablative coating is passive cooling, and a scramjet carries no liquid oxygen since it burns atmospheric oxygen.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 110-111; cooling principle is static

questions.q:
With reference to 'Mission Drishti', consider the following statements:
1. Its satellite carries a multispectral imager and a synthetic aperture radar on the same platform.
2. It was launched on ISRO's Small Satellite Launch Vehicle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. The satellite, built by an Indian start-up, is described as the first to fuse multispectral and radar imaging on one platform, giving pictures that are usable in all weather, by day and night, yet easy to read. Statement 2 is wrong: it was launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 into a sun-synchronous low Earth orbit. It is the largest privately built Indian Earth-observation satellite.

questions.q:
With reference to support for private space firms in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Rs 1,000 crore venture capital fund for space start-ups is managed by SIDBI.
2. The Technology Adoption Fund is meant to help commercialise early-stage innovations.
3. The Indian Space Association is the commercial arm of ISRO that transfers technologies such as the SSLV to industry.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The venture fund offers risk capital to individual start-ups because private investors avoid a sector with long gestation, and the adoption fund bridges the gap between prototype and product; a seed fund gives smaller grants. Statement 3 is wrong: the association is an industry body and policy voice of private firms. ISRO's commercial arm, which transfers launch-vehicle technology, is NewSpace India Limited.

questions.q: The report 'Ease of Doing Research & Development in India', released in 2026, was brought out by
o: the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser
the Department of Science and Technology
questions.e: NITI Aayog prepared the report, listing barriers in funding, human resources, institutional processes, technology transfer and access to knowledge, with recommendations for each. The other three bodies are all plausible because they shape science policy: the adviser's office coordinates across ministries, the research foundation funds projects, and the science department runs missions. The report in fact asks several of them to raise post-doctoral fellowships every year.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Venus, the target of an Indian mission planned for 2028:
1. It rotates in a direction opposite to that of most planets.
2. Its surface atmospheric pressure is about one-hundredth of that on the Earth.
3. It is the hottest planet of the Solar System even though Mercury is nearer the Sun.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; statement 2 is wrong. Venus spins slowly and backwards, taking about 243 Earth days to rotate once. Its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere causes a runaway greenhouse effect, so its surface is hotter than Mercury's. The same atmosphere is extremely dense: surface pressure is about ninety times that of the Earth, not a hundredth, which is why landers survive only briefly. Studying how Venus turned hostile helps in understanding Earth's climate.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 111; planetary facts are static

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order, from the earliest to the latest:
1. Launch of Vikram-S
2. Setting up of IN-SPACe
3. Approval of the Venus Orbiter Mission
4. Soft landing of Chandrayaan-3
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: IN-SPACe was created in 2020 as the single-window body for private players. Vikram-S flew in November 2022 as a result of that opening. Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, and the Venus mission was approved in 2024 for launch in 2028. The order shows reform first, then private launches, followed by ISRO's turn towards science and deep-space missions.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 103-105; Vision IAS pp. 111, 113

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A drone swarm can keep working even when some of its drones are shot down or its link with the ground station is jammed.
Statement-II: In a swarm, every drone is commanded individually and in real time by a single ground-based controller.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. A swarm survives losses because control is decentralised: the drones share data peer-to-peer, re-allocate tasks and re-form when some are destroyed, and they can continue even if the ground link is jammed. A single ground controller issuing every command would be exactly the point of failure that jamming exploits, so the description in Statement-II fits a remotely piloted fleet, not a swarm. The same autonomy raises concern about accountability for lethal decisions.

questions.q: 'POEM', a facility that ISRO offers to start-ups and research groups, is
o: a test stand at Sriharikota for firing private rocket engines
a ground station network leased to private satellite operators
a small satellite bus supplied to start-ups for their payloads
the spent fourth stage of the PSLV, kept in orbit as a platform for experiments
questions.e: The PSLV Orbital Experimental Module reuses the rocket's final stage, which would otherwise be debris, as a stabilised platform with power and communication, so that payloads can be tested in orbit cheaply. Satellite bus and ground station services are separate offerings to private firms, as is access to ISRO test facilities. Together with the technical centre at Ahmedabad they lower entry costs for start-ups that cannot build such infrastructure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Cell Broadcast System launched in 2026 can warn a large population faster than alerts sent by SMS.
Statement-II: A cell broadcast is transmitted at once to every handset within the targeted cells, without being addressed to individual numbers.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct and the second explains the first. An SMS is sent to each number in turn and queues up when the network is congested, which is exactly what happens in a disaster. A broadcast goes from the tower to all phones in the chosen area simultaneously, so it is quick and can be targeted geographically. The system is tied to the national alerting platform that follows the Common Alerting Protocol.

questions.q:
With reference to research and development in India, as discussed in NITI Aayog's 2026 report, consider the following statements:
1. India's gross expenditure on R&D is about 2 per cent of GDP.
2. The Government is the dominant source of R&D funding in India.
3. The report recommends that the entire increase in R&D spending should come from public funds.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. India spends roughly 0.65 per cent of GDP on research, far below the United States, China or South Korea; 2 per cent is the target the report sets for the next four to five years. Unlike those countries, where business leads, government funds most Indian research. The report therefore wants about half of the spending to come from the private sector, using CSR provisions and philanthropy.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of terms seen in astronomy news in 2026:
Term : Meaning
1. Zwan-Wolf effect : Squeezing of charged particles along magnetic flux tubes, which helps deflect the solar wind around a planet
2. Alfvenic kink waves : Transverse waves along magnetic field lines, proposed as a cause of the Sun's corona being hotter than its surface
3. Zone of Avoidance : Part of the sky hidden from view by the dust and stars of the Milky Way
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. The Zwan-Wolf effect was seen for the first time in a planetary atmosphere, that of Mars, using data from NASA's MAVEN orbiter. Kink waves shake coronal plasma sideways, and the turbulence may heat the corona to about a million degrees against some 5,500 degrees at the photosphere. The Zone of Avoidance is the roughly one-fifth of the sky obscured by our own galaxy; it hid the Vela Supercluster. A black hole's boundary is the event horizon, which is a different idea.
